title: Roadmap planning - inference runtime & launch readiness
summary: Internal roadmap and launch readiness meeting for the inference runtime's next quarter. Covered launch checklist, outstanding incidents/regressions, canary/rollout strategy, benchmarks for latency/cost, monitoring gaps, and required action items before GA. Decided to delay one non-critical feature (dynamic KV cache tuning) to post-launch and to run two 48-hour soak tests with canary traffic. Agreed owners and due dates for security sign-off and doc updates.
topics: Incident review: KV cache eviction bug

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-02-15
Start time: 09:30 PST
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Samira Patel, Jorge Alvarez, Priya Nair, Daniel Kim, Leah O'Connor, Tom Reynolds, Nina Brooks

Summary (auto): roadmap and launch readiness for inference runtime GA.

[00:00] Samira: ok, uh, let's kick off. thanks everyone for joining. goal today is to go through the launch checklist, the recent incident, and the rollout plan. we have about 55 minutes.
[00:28] Jorge: quick note — I posted the latest benchmark sheet in the #launch channel, link in notes, it's the run with quantized-fp16 and the new kernel selection heuristics. numbers look good but there's a latency tail at 95th for long contexts.
[00:46] Priya: and that's been popping in prod canary, yeah. the KV cache eviction race we saw last week caused a bunch of extra token re-computation which blew the tail.
[01:12] Daniel: i'm on that KV bug, i have a draft fix that serializes the eviction path but i'm still seeing a rare contention in stress tests. i want another day of debugging.
[01:36] Tom: what's the risk if we ship without that fix? are we likely to see customer impact?
[01:48] Daniel: risk is increased p95s under certain workload patterns — mainly many concurrent warm starts where the KV cache is being purged frequently. customers with long-context chat sessions could see doubled cost on those requests, so not ideal.
[02:12] Nina: so does that imply we delay GA? we need clarity on rollback and SLA exposure.
[02:26] Samira: proposal: keep GA but we gate some high-risk customers — do a staged canary 5/25/50% over two 48h soaks. if the fix lands before canary we include full traffic. if not, we exclude the long-context heavy tenants.
[02:52] Jorge: for the perf spreadsheet i added the cost-per-token delta for the quantized run; most customers see a 30-40% reduction but these long-context edge cases show up as outliers.
[03:18] Priya: monitoring note: we currently instrument cache miss ratio and evictions but not the end-to-end token re-gen metric — we should add a derived metric that counts re-generated tokens per request.
[03:42] Daniel: yeah i can add that to the telemetry. might take a day to wire up and validate the queries.
[03:54] Leah: for release we need the runbook updated with rollback steps — right now rollback is "flip config", but we need exact SLO thresholds to trigger rollback and a playbook for manual vs automated.
[04:12] Samira: add SLO thresholds: p95 latency > 450ms over 10 minutes OR regen-token-rate > 1% sustained for 15 minutes triggers manual rollback. automated rollback only for severe error rate spikes.
[04:36] Tom: are those numbers aligned with Dedicated SLA commitments? we can't silently violate partner contracts.
[04:48] Priya: Dedicated customers have slightly different SLOs; Leah, can you ensure the runbook has channel-specific thresholds?
[05:00] Leah: yes i'll template it.
[05:12] Samira: next item: security & compliance. Priya, where are we on KMS integration and SOC2 sign-off?
[05:26] Priya: KMS integration is in progress, keywrap testing done, awaiting the KMS secrets rotation policy to be signed by security. SOC2 docs — we completed most controls but external auditor scoping needs to be finalized. i'm targeting the 22nd for scoping doc.
[05:48] Samira: add as action item then.
[06:00] Jorge: on the kernel selector, one more note: the heuristics are slightly conservative for 8k+ sequences. for those we fall back to a safe path that is slower; we can relax after we have more perf data.
[06:18] Daniel: that fallback path also interacts with the batcher; the way we do continuous batching means requests might get different kernel decisions mid-inference which caused inconsistency in earlier runs.
[06:36] Samira: that's a launch risk for correctness — any chance it changes model outputs significantly?
[06:48] Daniel: it shouldn't change model outputs deterministically, but micro-timing differences could affect non-deterministic sampling. low prob but we should note in docs.
[07:06] Nina: on customer comms — we'll need a clear section in the release notes about known behavior and recommended prompt patterns for long contexts.
[07:22] Samira: agreed. Leah, add to release notes checklist.
[07:30] Leah: done.
[07:36] [08:00] Speaker 1: (mumble) can we talk about canary config?
[08:10] Jorge: yes. plan is: stage 1 internal traffic (10% synthetic load) for 6 hours smoke; stage 2 5% real traffic for 48 hours; stage 3 25% for 48 hours; stage 4 full if no regressions. each stage has health gates: p95, error rate, regen-token-rate.
[08:40] Priya: and we need automated alerts to Slack + PagerDuty on gate failures. right now alerts only to Slack — i'll add PD policies.
[09:02] Daniel: CI/perf — after the patch, runs will go through our perf harness; i want to see 3 runs with identical seeds to check for flakiness.
[09:18] Samira: what about cost controls? we have customers concerned about per-token cost — how are we presenting quantization tradeoffs?
[09:32] Jorge: the Optimize toolkit will recommend quantization profiles per workload. for launch, we present a comparison: accuracy delta < 1% for most tasks, cost down 30-40%. still need to flag long-context cases.
[09:52] Tom: also tie this to routing policy — we can route sensitive customers to higher-precision variants or to Dedicated pools.
[10:06] Nina: timeline check — what's the agreed GA date if we pass canary?
[10:12] Samira: target GA is 2025-03-03, but that's contingent on the canary ok and SOC2 scoping.
[10:22] Priya: if the KV fix slips, we can still GA but with a reduced rollout and a clear mitigation plan. decision point is 48 hours before GA.
[10:36] Daniel: the PR should be ready by tomorrow EOD; it's just failing one stress.
[10:44] [11:10] Speaker 2: (inaudible) we've got some outstanding perf regression alerts from last night — Jorge will follow up with the perf team.
[11:28] Jorge: i'll take that. i'm also going to annotate the spreadsheet with tenant-level breakdowns so we can decide exclusion lists for canary.
[11:40] Leah: ops checklist — we need traffic labels, canary runbooks, escalation owners, and the postmortem template updated. I'll combine and share a single checklist doc.
[12:00] Samira: who's owning the tenant exclusion list?
[12:06] Jorge: i'll propose one by tomorrow, Priya to vet for monitoring coverage.
[12:16] Nina: do we have legal/compliance sign-off for the launch comms? any data residency constraints?
[12:28] Priya: not yet, but dedicated customers often require region pinning. that's in the launch notes. legal needs to sign off on the customer-facing release notes for EU/ANZ customers.
[12:44] Samira: action: Priya to coordinate with legal.
[12:48] [13:30] Daniel: on incident review, quick recap — last week's KV eviction race: sequence of events: 1) heavy concurrent warm starts, 2) background cache compaction kicked in, 3) eviction lock contention caused duplicate fetches, 4) regen tokens spiked.
[13:58] Daniel: root cause is the compaction task not respecting in-flight request markers. fix is to check and skip eviction when markers present.
[14:12] Priya: mitigation is rate-limit compaction and add backpressure when eviction runs are high.
[14:24] Samira: that sounds good — Daniel push a hotfix, Priya add compaction throttling.
[14:36] Daniel: will do.
[14:42] Tom: any follow-up from customers impacted?
[14:48] Leah: we sent an incident note to affected accounts and offered assist; response has been ok but one customer asked for a deeper postmortem.
[14:58] Samira: let's prepare a postmortem draft by 02/20. Leah own.
[15:06] Leah: noted.
[15:12] [15:40] Speaker 3: (crosstalk) are we blocking on any external team?
[15:46] Jorge: kernel team might need extra cycles if we relax heuristics; they're in the loop but need a decision by Friday.
[15:58] Samira: decision owner Jorge to finalize kernel relaxation plan Friday.
[16:06] Nina: any known regression risk with S3-backed KV cache for on-prem?
[16:18] Daniel: on-prem S3 implementations vary, but we plan to ship with a compatibility matrix. some customers will need custom tuning.
[16:30] Priya: also we need to document our recommended S3 configs in Private deployment docs.
[16:40] Samira: Leah add that to docs checklist.
[16:48] [17:10] Speaker 1: (voices) ok time check — 20 minutes left; summarize decisions please.
[17:20] Samira: decisions: 1) GA target stays 2025-03-03 with guardrails, 2) KV fix is high priority but GA can proceed with staged rollout if fix isn't in, 3) add regen-token metric and PD alerts, 4) run two 48-hour canary soaks, 5) delay dynamic KV tuning feature to after GA.
[17:38] Jorge: i'll share updated benchmarks and tenant breakdown.
[17:46] Priya: i'll finish SOC2 scoping and KMS checklist by 02/22.
[17:54] Daniel: i'll land the hotfix PR and run stress tests.
[18:04] Leah: runbooks, postmortem draft, and release notes updates targeted by 02/20-02/21.
[18:14] Samira: OK, any last questions?
[18:20] Tom: just make sure the decision point is explicit — 48h before GA we either expand or restrict the rollout based on canary data.
[18:32] Samira: noted. thanks everyone. we'll reconvene in the next check-in on Monday unless blockers pop up.

End of transcript.

References shared: perf spreadsheet (link: https://rels.example.com/launch/perf-q2), runbook draft (internal link), incident doc (internal link).
